rootCause.defect: For functions in NO_SERVICE_ROLE_EXECUTE the generator emitted only the comment '-- deliberately NOT granted to service_role: an internal lock helper, not an entry point.' and no revoke.
rootCause.mechanism: Supabase carries `alter default privileges in schema public grant execute on functions to service_role`, so CREATE FUNCTION grants service_role EXECUTE DIRECTLY. The generated `revoke ... from public` cannot remove a directly-held privilege. Bare PostgreSQL has no such default, so service_role only ever held EXECUTE via PUBLIC — which is why scripts/por1/rehearse-promotion.sh and tests/por1/catalogue-baseline.sh passed while the first real Supabase apply failed.
rootCause.provenanceOfCorrectBehaviour: The Preview lineage 202607310002 revokes the helper from public, anon, authenticated AND service_role by hand. The compiler re-derives grants rather than copying them (deliberate — the Preview grants had a real hole, see 202608010001) and lost that fourth revoke in translation.
rootCause.assertionWasCorrect: 202608010108 was right to refuse; the fix is upstream of it and the assertion is unchanged.
